## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Error IDs can be paired with the wrong nodestore payloads

Affected:
- src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:107-120

Explanation:
`nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict keyed by node ID. The code then zips `error_ids` with `events.values()` and assumes both are in the same order and the same length. If a backend omits missing keys, or returns them in a different order, every following error gets the wrong ID and possibly the wrong title or message.

There is a second gap: node IDs are built with the endpoint's `project.id`. A replay's errors can come from other projects, and those errors will silently be missing.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
node_ids = {Event.generate_node_id(project_id, event_id=eid): eid for eid in error_ids}
events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(list(node_ids))
return [
    ErrorEvent(category="error", id=node_ids[nid], title=data.get("title", ""),
               timestamp=data.get("timestamp", 0.0), message=data.get("message", ""))
    for nid, data in events.items() if data is not None
]
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Error timestamps (seconds) are compared with rrweb event timestamps (milliseconds)

Affected:
- src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:149-158

Explanation:
Error `timestamp` values from nodestore are epoch seconds (floats). Top-level rrweb recording event `timestamp` values are normally epoch milliseconds. With `error_ts < event.get("timestamp", 0)`, every error will sort before the first breadcrumb. This defeats the stated goal of placing errors in chronological order.

The unit test passes only because it uses small, hand-picked values in the same unit. Normalize both sides to one unit before comparing.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
event_ts = event.get("timestamp", 0)
if event_ts > 1e11:  # ms -> s
    event_ts /= 1000
while error_idx < len(error_events) and error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event_ts:
    ...
~~~

## 3) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: User-supplied `field` params can drop `error_ids` from the replay lookup

Affected:
- src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:79-84

Explanation:
`process_raw_response` filters its output to the fields the caller requested. Any client that passes `field=` without `error_ids` will silently get no error context. Since this lookup is internal, pass a fixed field list instead of the caller's query parameters.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
response = process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=["error_ids"])
~~~

## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Hidden span attributes are only filtered when a search query is present

Affected:
- static/app/views/performance/newTraceDetails/traceDrawer/details/span/eapSections/attributes.tsx:62-69

Explanation:
The early `return sorted;` runs when `searchQuery` is empty. So `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` (`is_segment`, `project_id`, `received`) are still shown in the default, unsearched view. That is the common case, so the feature mostly does nothing. The filter needs to apply before the early return.

Proposed fix:
~~~tsx
const visible = sorted.filter(a => !HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(a.name));
if (!searchQuery) return visible;
return visible.filter(a => a.name.toLowerCase().trim().includes(searchQuery.toLowerCase().trim()));
~~~

## 5) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Feature-flagged table widget always renders an empty table

Affected:
- static/app/views/dashboards/widgetCard/chart.tsx:164-175

Explanation:
When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, `TableWidgetVisualization` receives `columns={[]}` and empty `tableData`. The actual `result.data` and `result.meta` are ignored, and the loading state is not handled. Any organization with the flag on will see blank dashboard tables.

Either wire up the real data or keep the old table until part 2 lands.

Proposed fix:
~~~tsx
<TableWidgetVisualization
  tableData={{data: result.data, meta: {fields: result.meta?.fields ?? {}, units: result.meta?.units ?? {}}}}
/>
~~~

## 6) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Attribute-keys query cache key omits the organization

Affected:
- static/app/views/explore/hooks/useTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx:30-42

Explanation:
The new `useQuery` key is `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]`, and `queryOptions` contains neither the organization slug nor the URL. When the project selection is empty (all projects) and the datetime matches, two organizations produce the same key. After switching orgs, the cache can serve the previous organization's attributes.

The old `useApiQuery` key included the org-scoped path. Separately, `retry: false`, `staleTime: 0` and `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` were dropped, which changes refetch behavior.

Proposed fix:
~~~tsx
const queryKey = useMemo(
  () => ['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', organization.slug, queryOptions],
  [organization.slug, queryOptions]
);
~~~

## 7) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Mutual-exclusion check for age/timestamp misses falsy values

Affected:
- src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:50-60

Explanation:
`self.initial_data.get("age")` is falsy when `age` is 0, which is a valid Editor's Draft value. A report with both `timestamp` and `age: 0` is therefore accepted, and the same applies to `timestamp: 0`. A report with neither field also passes validation.

Use key presence checks instead, ideally in a single `validate()` method.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
def validate(self, attrs):
    has_age, has_ts = "age" in self.initial_data, "timestamp" in self.initial_data
    if has_age == has_ts:
        raise serializers.ValidationError("Exactly one of age or timestamp must be present")
    return attrs
~~~

## 8) Severity: LOW | Type: Implementation
Title: Analytics recorded before the feature-flag check

Affected:
- src/sentry/preprod/api/endpoints/organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py:81-86

Explanation:
`preprod_artifact.api.assemble` is recorded before the `features.has` check. Requests that are rejected (feature disabled) are counted as assembles, which inflates the metrics the dashboard is meant to show. Move the call after the feature and permission checks.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
if not features.has(...):
    return Response(..., status=403)
analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)
~~~

## 9) Severity: LOW | Type: Performance
Title: Per-issue recommended-event lookup when building PR comments

Affected:
- src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py:584-597

Explanation:
`get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for every issue. That is a Snuba query plus a nodestore fetch per issue, run sequentially inside the comment task.

Separately, issue titles and environment names are interpolated into Markdown link text and backticks without escaping. A title containing `]` or `` ` `` can break or alter the rendered comment.

Proposed fix:
~~~python
# Escape markdown in title/env
safe_title = re.sub(r"([\[\]`*_])", r"\\\1", truncated_title)
~~~

## 10) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: No-op migrations reference a migration not included in this change

Affected:
- src/sentry/migrations/0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py:14-16
- src/sentry/migrations/0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised.py:13-15

Explanation:
Both data migrations are now no-ops and point to `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py`, which does not appear in this diff. If 0921 is not present on this branch, environments that have not yet applied 0917/0920 will never convert org saved searches to views. It may come from one of the commits not shown, so this needs confirming rather than assuming it is missing.

Proposed fix:
~~~text
Ensure 0921 lands in the same deploy (or before) this change.
~~~

## 11) Severity: LOW | Type: Style
Title: Flex refactor dropped alignment, gap and height styles

Affected:
- static/app/views/performance/newTraceDetails/traceTabsAndVitals.tsx:93
- static/app/views/performance/newTraceDetails/traceWaterfall.tsx:712
- static/app/components/events/eventAttachments.tsx:143

Explanation:
These replacements are not behavior-preserving:
- **`traceTabsAndVitals.tsx`:** the old `Container` had `align-items: center` and `gap: space(1)`; the new `<Flex justify="space-between">` has neither.
- **`traceWaterfall.tsx`:** the old `FlexBox` had `height: 100%`, which is dropped.
- **`eventAttachments.tsx`:** the old `FlexCenter` applied `overflowEllipsis`; the new `Flex` does not, so long attachment names may overflow their grid cell.

Proposed fix:
~~~tsx
<Flex ref={setRef} justify="space-between" align="center" gap={space(1)}>
~~~
